note: Montserrat, read on 2026-10-30 on the Government of Montserrat's pages (gov.ms): its services page for work permits and the Office of the Deputy Governor's guidance on a Permit of Permanent Residence under the Immigration (Permanent Residence Permits) Regulations 2005 (a leaflet uploaded in August 2020). This replaces the file held in wave 8, which read the work permit as tied to the employer, as applied for from either place, its $125 fee as Eastern Caribbean dollars and a renewal's two weeks as the decision time, and the permanent permit as applied for in Montserrat and allowing any work: none of these is written now. Work permits are applied for and renewed through the Department of Labour; a variation to a new employer takes Form 'A'; the processing fee is EC$75 for a CARICOM national and '$125.00' for others (the currency of the second not printed, so no fee is written), before a final payment for the permit that the page doesn't state; a renewal or variation usually takes two weeks (not a first permit's time, so not written). A Permit of Permanent Residence may be asked of the Governor on the advice of Cabinet by a person ordinarily resident in Montserrat for the eight years immediately before applying (residence begun on or after 1 January 2003; five for residence begun before, not written), gainfully employed the last six months, with savings averaging $5,000 or property worth $50,000, absent no more than 90 days in any year; it is written as 8 years on the work permit (a reading: the regulations count ordinary residence, which the page doesn't tie to a permit). The application is made on form 'S' from the Office of the Deputy Governor in Brades and the prescribed fee is paid to the Accountant General on approval; the fee isn't stated, nor where an applicant must be, nor what work it allows. OECS citizens' freedom to work (the work engine's) isn't a residence route here.
